summary: Internal incident review focused on a regression observed in the recent staging rollout that increased tail latency for long-context requests and surfaced a tokenization discrepancy for a subset of models. Team aligned on immediate mitigations, canary timing, and owners for root cause work and QA sweeps.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Carlos, Priya, Ethan, Lina, Noah, Sofia

[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is the incident review for the staging rollout yesterday, let's uh kick off with a quick timeline from Carlos.
[00:18] Carlos: yeah sure, so at 14:12 UTC staging started the v1.13 deployment, we saw increased 95/99 latency around 14:45 UTC, by 15:05 we started seeing tokenization mismatches on some internal prompts, most notably when sequence > 8k, the KV-cache warm path looked fine but the continuous batching path had spikes.
[00:44] Priya: to add, the alerting threshold at 14:40 fired for tail latency, then ops escalated. We routed traffic to fallback model variant (v1.12-q4) which reduced error rates but costs went up due to smaller batch efficiency.
[01:05] Ethan: quick note, the tokenization diff seems tied to the tokenizer update shipped in the model-ops pack; probably mismatch in BPE indices when using the quantized kernel. I was able to reproduce locally with a synthetic long prompt.
[01:28] Lina: is this the same thing we saw in the benchmarking spreadsheet — the weird off-by-one token occasionally?
[01:35] Noah: yep i saw that in the e2e tests, sometimes a trailing space becomes a different token and downstream parsing for structured outputs fails, so that explains the regression alerts.
[01:48] Maya: rough numbers, production-like staging had ~8% of requests with 99th > 2s for long-context traces, and error uplift of 0.6% for the retriever pipeline. Not catastrophic but enough to block GA.
[02:07] Sofia: and that error spike popped up during our planned capacity pressure test which magnified batching inefficiencies. We should call out the test as a contributing factor.
[02:20] Carlos: timeline wise, we rolled back to v1.12 at 16:10 UTC after rollback failed-first attempts with a partial manual divert. Rollback restored baseline latency by 16:32.
[02:36] Maya: okay let's capture root cause hypotheses: tokenizer change + quantized kernel incompatibility, batching scheduler regressions for long sequences, and capacity-pressure test exposed the corner case. prioritize which to chase first?
[02:52] Ethan: tokenizer + kernel mismatch is highest priority, I can dig into the model-ops artifacts and compare token id maps. I suspect a packaging mismatch where the tokenizer was updated but the quantization mapping stayed stale.
[03:07] Priya: i'll look at runtime metrics — KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, and the scheduler's latency distribution. If batching collapsed into smaller effective batches under pressure that would explain per-token cost increase.
[03:22] Lina: i'll update the launch checklist to add an explicit tokenization checksum and a long-context smoke test before cutover. Also will surface the canary acceptance criteria around 99th percentile.
[03:36] Carlos: quick clarifying q, is the tokenizer change from our team or from the upstream model repo?
[03:42] Ethan: it's from the model-ops pipeline, but we applied a patch to the BPE table during last-week's merge, so it's internal but surfaced via the packaging step.
[03:50] Maya: any security or compliance concern? KMS rotations or key access changed?
[03:55] Priya: not related to KMS for this incident, but while inspecting i noticed KMS rotation logs for one private customer test that failed auth when we toggled the key version; i'll follow up separately — not a blocker for launch but a risk.
[04:12] Sofia: we need a canary plan: short window, small traffic percentage, and fast rollback. I propose start with 2% for 1 hour, monitor 95/99, tokenization diffs, and user-visible regression tests. If stable, 10% next day. Thoughts?
[04:35] Carlos: sounds good. Add safety net: auto-divert to v1.12 if 99th latency > 1.5s or token diffs > 0.2%.
[04:46] Maya: okay include that. Also, is there a plan for a deeper perf run to isolate batching behavior?
[04:52] Priya: yes, i'll run a controlled perf test with long contexts and vary batch scheduler knobs; will test on the same hardware profile as prod (A100 equivalent).
[05:03] Noah: QA will run the full e2e, including travis-like smoke for structured output parsing, and a set of golden prompts. i'm adding cold-start scenarios too.
[05:18] Ethan: one more item — some logs show kernel selection took a fallback path which added 200ms per token in the worst cases, likely due to the quantized kernel rejecting a fused op. i'll add kernel selection traces.
[05:34] Lina: can we add a preflight in the deploy pipeline that runs a tokenization checksum and a fast perf probe? That would have caught this.
[05:44] Carlos: yes we can — it's a short step: run token-checksum + run 10 long-context synthetic requests and check 99th < threshold.
[05:55] Maya: ok let's enumerate mitigation actions for the next 48 hours. Ethan will own tokenization root cause, Priya owns perf/batching investigation, Noah owns QA sweep, Sofia will own canary/rollback docs, Lina will update checklist, Maya will prepare postmortem.
[06:18] (brief crosstalk)
[06:24] Priya: i want to call out that when the capacity-pressure test ran, autoscaler briefly overshot and we ended up in a smaller-batch mode which reduced batching efficiency. We should tune the autoscaler cooldowns so we don't oscillate under controlled load tests.
[06:40] Carlos: noted — autoscaler tuning item added. Also we should make the canary gating automated so engineers don't rely on manual slides.
[06:50] Sofia: i'll draft the automated gating playbook, with explicit metrics and who to notify on fail.
[06:58] Maya: good. Any blockers to proceeding with the canary next week?
[07:03] Ethan: i need at least 36 hours to reproduce and confirm the token id mapping fix locally, so that pushes canary to 2026-08-24 earliest.
[07:11] Lina: that's fine — we'll shift timeline but keep launch window.
[07:15] Maya: final wrap, let's confirm owners and due dates. We'll reconvene in two days for a checkpoint (2026-08-20) and then run the canary on 2026-08-24 if all green.
[07:30] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: some proper nouns may be misheard (e.g., "Dedictaed" for Dedicated, "KV cash" for KV cache). There are a few overlaps and filler words left in to reflect verbatim transcript style.
